# GitHub Repository Governance & Branch Protection Settings

`main` is protected by a **ruleset**, not by classic branch protection, and that ruleset is
applied by tooling rather than by hand. Editing **Settings → Branches** here has no effect; the
rules live under **Settings → Rules → Rulesets**, in one named *Main Branch Governance Ruleset*.

That ruleset is generated by `align_repo_conventions.py` in
[rtkelly13/shared-utilities](https://github.com/rtkelly13/shared-utilities)
(`src/shared_utilities/repo_governance/`), which applies the same shape across every repository it
manages. **Change the settings there, not here** — running `enforce` against this repo overwrites
anything set by hand.

This file describes what that ruleset actually configures. It previously described a stricter
policy than the tool applies, which is worth avoiding: a governance document that disagrees with
the enforcement is worse than none, because it is trusted.

---

## 🔒 1. Ruleset on `main`

Applied with `enforcement: active`, targeting `refs/heads/main`.

- **Pull request required before merging**
  - Required approving reviews: **0**. Merging does not wait for a reviewer.
  - Stale reviews are dismissed on push.
  - Code Owner review: **not required**. `.github/CODEOWNERS` still requests reviewers
    automatically, but nothing blocks on their approval.
  - Unresolved review threads **do** block merging.
- **Required status checks** — these are **job** names, not workflow names. GitHub Actions reports
  one check per job, so requiring a workflow name means the check never reports and every pull
  request blocks indefinitely on "N of N required status checks are expected", with nothing naming
  what it is waiting for:
    - `build` (`ci.yml`)
    - `pr-title` (`pr-title.yml`)
  - These two strings are an API between the workflows here and
    `REPO_REQUIRED_CHECKS_MAP` in shared-utilities. Renaming a job silently breaks the ruleset, so
    rename the job and update that map in the same change. An earlier pair of long descriptive
    names containing `&` and parentheses caused exactly the failure above.
  - Do **not** require the benchmark workflow. It is `workflow_dispatch` only, so it would never
    report a status.
  - **Strict mode is on** (`strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`), meaning a branch must be
    up to date with `main` before merging. Every merge therefore invalidates every other open pull
    request, which forces a rebase-and-rerun each time. That is painful while a queue of Dependabot
    pull requests is open, and is the setting to relax first if merges start serialising.
- **Linear history required**, so squash or rebase merges only.
- **Branch deletion and force pushes blocked.**

---

## 🔀 2. Pull Request & Merge Strategy Settings

Navigate to **Settings → General → Pull Requests**:

- [x] **Allow squash merging**: **ENABLED**
  - Default commit message: *Pull request title and description*
- [ ] **Allow merge commits**: **DISABLED** (enforces clean linear history)
- [ ] **Allow rebase merging**: **DISABLED** (or enabled if rebase is preferred)
- [x] **Automatically delete head branches**: **ENABLED**
  - Automatically deletes feature branches after PR merge to keep the repository clean.

---

## 🛡️ 3. Security & Dependency Analysis

Navigate to **Settings → Code security and analysis**:

- [x] **Dependency graph**: Enabled
- [x] **Dependabot alerts**: Enabled
- [x] **Dependabot security updates**: Enabled
- [x] **Secret scanning**: Enabled
